Rebuilds the global header per SFCC-52 and its successor stories (SFCC-746 nav bar, SFCC-747 logo). Built as six independently-implemented branches, merged for integrated local testing, plus follow-on Contentful and i18n work done directly on this branch once testing surfaced real gaps.

**Header build (six merged branches):**
- **Beta cherry-pick + cleanup** — `LeftBar`/`RightBar`/`ZimmSearchInput` header decomposition (from `feature/SFCC-52_global-header-ui-beta`), dead `navGroup/` removed.
- **`header-css-tokens`** — co-located `header.ts`/`listMenu.ts` recipes to `header.css.ts`/`list-menu.css.ts`, fixed `NAV_LETTER_SPACING` to `0` per confirmed Figma token.
- **`contentful-navgroup-migration`** — generalised footer's `footerNavGroup` into a shared `navGroup` type (footer + header mega-menu columns); live Contentful `dev` migrated.
- **`sfcc-746-nav-bar`** (SFCC-746) — new `headerNavItem`/`headerNavigation` Contentful types, `useHeaderNav` hook, `ListMenu` self-fetches nav data (placeholder content component pending SFCC-96).
- **`sfcc-747-logo`** (SFCC-747) — fixed header rendering the base template's placeholder icon instead of the real `ZimmLogo` wordmark; verified AC (focus, keyboard, responsive sizing, no Contentful dependency).
- **`header-shell-tests`** — backfilled missing Storybook/Vitest coverage for `LeftBar`/`RightBar`/`list-menu.tsx`/`list-menu-trigger.tsx`.
- **`header-menu-expanded-state`** — shared `MenuExpandedState` contract (`closed`/`fullSwap`/`mobileL1`/`mobileL2`) wired into `LeftBar`/`RightBar`, demoed via Storybook mock toggles.

**Contentful — properly reconciled, not just dev-patched:**
- Merged `feature/contentful-cleanup` (CodeRabbit-approved) — brings `image.js` into the tracked content-types set and removes several dead Contentful components (`button`, `duplexSection`, `collectionHero`, `imageText`, `heroBanner`, `productHero`, `videoEmbed`).
- Added `phoneLabel`/`whatsAppLabel`/`emailLabel` to `footerConfig` (co-located with existing `phoneHref`/`whatsAppHref`/`emailHref` — one editorial unit, not a generic microcopy string), wired through `Footer` → `FooterNavColumn` → `ZimmContactIconRow`.
- Ran a full `sync:contentful` + `install:contentful --target dev` — the org-level Environment Template is now properly version-6, covering `footerConfig`/`headerNavItem`/`headerNavigation`/`image`/`link`/`navGroup`/`region`/`uiCopy`. `navGroup`/`headerNavItem`/`headerNavigation` (previously dev-only via direct API writes) are now genuinely template-managed.
- Closed out the deferred `footerNavGroup` cleanup — hard-deleted the 3 old entries and the content type itself now that `navGroup` fully supersedes it.
- Seeded live `dev` entries so the header renders real nav content end-to-end: 1 `headerNavigation` root + 5 `headerNavItem`s (New/Clothing/Accessories/Collections/Z.Immerse, all direct links).

**i18n — react-intl → uiCopy for Zimmermann-authored chrome:**
- New project policy: react-intl is out for Zimmermann-authored code, all aria-labels/UI chrome text source from Contentful's `uiCopy` type via `useUiCopy()` instead.
- Converted `header/index.tsx`, `leftBar/index.tsx`, `rightBar/index.tsx`, `list-menu/list-menu.tsx` — every `intl.formatMessage({id, defaultMessage})` became `t(key, fallback)`, same key/fallback text, so behaviour is unchanged until an editor overrides a value.
- Extended `useUiCopy`'s `t()` with optional `values` interpolation support (react-intl had this, `uiCopy` didn't — needed for `"My cart, number of items: {numItems}"`).
- Replaced `rightBar`'s direct read of vendor SFCC react-intl content (`messages[link.name]` from `@salesforce/retail-react-app`'s `account/constant.js`) with a local `ACCOUNT_NAV_LABELS` map, so nothing in this component calls `formatMessage` on someone else's descriptors anymore.
- Fixed 6 missing `header.button.assistive_msg.*` translation keys along the way (pre-existing gap, console-warning only, not a behaviour bug).

## Explicitly NOT in this PR — still to do

- **SFCC-93 (scroll behaviour)** — no design AC exists yet; deliberately out of scope.
- **Header region selector** and **3 logo behaviour scenarios (HPC-016)** — no Figma frame provided, out of scope per the implementation plan.

## Known follow-ups (not blocking, flagged for visibility)

- `list-menu.stories.tsx` (from `header-shell-tests`) still tests/demos the old `root`/`categories` prop shape — `ListMenu` now self-fetches via `useHeaderNav()` and ignores those props, so this story renders incorrectly. Needs a rewrite.
- `RightBar`'s Wishlist/Account icon calls commerce hooks directly (`withRegistration`), despite its own JSDoc claiming container/presentational separation — throws without a `CommerceApiProvider` in the tree. Worth a second look before SFCC-96/97 build further on top of it.
- `gallery`/`galleryItem`/`imageAndText` Contentful types exist live in `dev` but are deliberately excluded from the tracked template — a BA's and Tim's own separate testing, not part of this initiative.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npm run test` — 22/22 files, 305/305 tests passing
- [x] Verified locally end-to-end: header renders real Contentful-driven nav data, logo/letter-spacing fixes visible, `menuExpanded` states demoed in Storybook (`Layout/Header/LeftBar`, `Layout/Header/RightBar`)
- [x] Live Contentful `dev` verified directly against the CDA (not just the app) after the template rebuild and content seeding
- [ ] Local CodeRabbit review (`cr review --light --base develop`) — not yet run on the merged integration branch
- [ ] Manual cross-breakpoint pass (desktop/tablet/mobile) once SFCC-96/97 land

block (pending HPC-018 resolution) still references intl.formatMessage

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016GTGo4ZCJGFzLwjsqmwitY","messageHeadline":"fix(header): set logo to fixed per-breakpoint dimensions","oid":"61f756ed3bfd321a5828e81930bdd2e9b245fdf8"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-26T23:49:23Z","authors":[{"email":"tim+1@lavelle.bio","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjY0NDU3MTA=","login":"TimLavelle","name":"TimLavelle"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Sonnet 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-26T23:49:23Z","messageBody":"Three compounding bugs, found and fixed in sequence while matching
the logo to Figma's 223x26 mobile / 758x115 tablet+desktop spec:

1. ZimmLogo took a plain DOM `style` prop, which can only ever hold
   one unconditional value — passing a Chakra responsive array through
   it just stringified to garbage ("223px,,758px,12"). ZimmLogo now
   renders via chakra.svg and accepts an `sx` prop (Chakra's own
   style-prop system, which actually resolves responsive values into
   real media queries) alongside the existing `style` for simple
   static overrides.
2. Even through `sx`, sizing still lost to base SFCC's own `logo` part
   (width: [8,8,8,12] Chakra-spacing array) at md/lg — Chakra's
   multi-part recipe merge combines our Header.css.ts override with
   that base part in a way that isn't a reliable per-key override for
   this specific key, regardless of array vs. fully-named-object
   responsive syntax. Logo sizing now bypasses that merge entirely:
   removed from header.css.ts's `logo` part, set instead as a plain
   HEADER_LOGO_SX object passed directly to <ZimmLogo sx={...}> in
   header/index.tsx — a plain object spread, no base theme involved.
3. ZimmLogo's own base sx sets maxWidth: 327px as a generic default,
   which survived the merge with HEADER_LOGO_SX (that object only set
   width/height) and silently capped the 758px desktop/tablet target.
   HEADER_LOGO_SX now explicitly sets maxWidth: 'none'.

1	{"additions":10187,"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjI5NDcyOTg2","is_bot":false,"login":"TimLavelleACC","name":""},"baseRefName":"develop","baseRefOid":"269d5d40149b9947111dd87e78d37b92fccd4c99","body":"## Summary

Rebuilds the global header per SFCC-52 and its successor stories (SFCC-746 nav bar, SFCC-747 logo). Built as six independently-implemented branches, merged for integrated local testing, plus follow-on Contentful and i18n work done directly on this branch once testing surfaced real gaps.

**Header build (six merged branches):**
- **Beta cherry-pick + cleanup** — `LeftBar`/`RightBar`/`ZimmSearchInput` header decomposition (from `feature/SFCC-52_global-header-ui-beta`), dead `navGroup/` removed.
- **`header-css-tokens`** — co-located `header.ts`/`listMenu.ts` recipes to `header.css.ts`/`list-menu.css.ts`, fixed `NAV_LETTER_SPACING` to `0` per confirmed Figma token.
- **`contentful-navgroup-migration`** — generalised footer's `footerNavGroup` into a shared `navGroup` type (footer + header mega-menu columns); live Contentful `dev` migrated.
- **`sfcc-746-nav-bar`** (SFCC-746) — new `headerNavItem`/`headerNavigation` Contentful types, `useHeaderNav` hook, `ListMenu` self-fetches nav data (placeholder content component pending SFCC-96).
- **`sfcc-747-logo`** (SFCC-747) — fixed header rendering the base template's placeholder icon instead of the real `ZimmLogo` wordmark; verified AC (focus, keyboard, responsive sizing, no Contentful dependency).
- **`header-shell-tests`** — backfilled missing Storybook/Vitest coverage for `LeftBar`/`RightBar`/`list-menu.tsx`/`list-menu-trigger.tsx`.
- **`header-menu-expanded-state`** — shared `MenuExpandedState` contract (`closed`/`fullSwap`/`mobileL1`/`mobileL2`) wired into `LeftBar`/`RightBar`, demoed via Storybook mock toggles.

**Contentful — properly reconciled, not just dev-patched:**
- Merged `feature/contentful-cleanup` (CodeRabbit-approved) — brings `image.js` into the tracked content-types set and removes several dead Contentful components (`button`, `duplexSection`, `collectionHero`, `imageText`, `heroBanner`, `productHero`, `videoEmbed`).
- Added `phoneLabel`/`whatsAppLabel`/`emailLabel` to `footerConfig` (co-located with existing `phoneHref`/`whatsAppHref`/`emailHref` — one editorial unit, not a generic microcopy string), wired through `Footer` → `FooterNavColumn` → `ZimmContactIconRow`.
- Ran a full `sync:contentful` + `install:contentful --target dev` — the org-level Environment Template is now properly version-6, covering `footerConfig`/`headerNavItem`/`headerNavigation`/`image`/`link`/`navGroup`/`region`/`uiCopy`. `navGroup`/`headerNavItem`/`headerNavigation` (previously dev-only via direct API writes) are now genuinely template-managed.
- Closed out the deferred `footerNavGroup` cleanup — hard-deleted the 3 old entries and the content type itself now that `navGroup` fully supersedes it.
- Seeded live `dev` entries so the header renders real nav content end-to-end: 1 `headerNavigation` root + 5 `headerNavItem`s (New/Clothing/Accessories/Collections/Z.Immerse, all direct links).

**i18n — react-intl → uiCopy for Zimmermann-authored chrome:**
- New project policy: react-intl is out for Zimmermann-authored code, all aria-labels/UI chrome text source from Contentful's `uiCopy` type via `useUiCopy()` instead.
- Converted `header/index.tsx`, `leftBar/index.tsx`, `rightBar/index.tsx`, `list-menu/list-menu.tsx` — every `intl.formatMessage({id, defaultMessage})` became `t(key, fallback)`, same key/fallback text, so behaviour is unchanged until an editor overrides a value.
- Extended `useUiCopy`'s `t()` with optional `values` interpolation support (react-intl had this, `uiCopy` didn't — needed for `"My cart, number of items: {numItems}"`).
- Replaced `rightBar`'s direct read of vendor SFCC react-intl content (`messages[link.name]` from `@salesforce/retail-react-app`'s `account/constant.js`) with a local `ACCOUNT_NAV_LABELS` map, so nothing in this component calls `formatMessage` on someone else's descriptors anymore.
- Fixed 6 missing `header.button.assistive_msg.*` translation keys along the way (pre-existing gap, console-warning only, not a behaviour bug).

## Explicitly NOT in this PR — still to do

- **SFCC-93 (scroll behaviour)** — no design AC exists yet; deliberately out of scope.
- **Header region selector** and **3 logo behaviour scenarios (HPC-016)** — no Figma frame provided, out of scope per the implementation plan.

## Known follow-ups (not blocking, flagged for visibility)

- `list-menu.stories.tsx` (from `header-shell-tests`) still tests/demos the old `root`/`categories` prop shape — `ListMenu` now self-fetches via `useHeaderNav()` and ignores those props, so this story renders incorrectly. Needs a rewrite.
- `RightBar`'s Wishlist/Account icon calls commerce hooks directly (`withRegistration`), despite its own JSDoc claiming container/presentational separation — throws without a `CommerceApiProvider` in the tree. Worth a second look before SFCC-96/97 build further on top of it.
- `gallery`/`galleryItem`/`imageAndText` Contentful types exist live in `dev` but are deliberately excluded from the tracked template — a BA's and Tim's own separate testing, not part of this initiative.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npm run test` — 22/22 files, 305/305 tests passing
- [x] Verified locally end-to-end: header renders real Contentful-driven nav data, logo/letter-spacing fixes visible, `menuExpanded` states demoed in Storybook (`Layout/Header/LeftBar`, `Layout/Header/RightBar`)
- [x] Live Contentful `dev` verified directly against the CDA (not just the app) after the template rebuild and content seeding
- [ ] Local CodeRabbit review (`cr review --light --base develop`) — not yet run on the merged integration branch
- [ ] Manual cross-breakpoint pass (desktop/tablet/mobile) once SFCC-96/97 land

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016GTGo4ZCJGFzLwjsqmwitY","messageHeadline":"fix(header): set logo to fixed per-breakpoint dimensions","oid":"61f756ed3bfd321a5828e81930bdd2e9b245fdf8"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-26T23:49:23Z","authors":[{"email":"tim+1@lavelle.bio","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjY0NDU3MTA=","login":"TimLavelle","name":"TimLavelle"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Sonnet 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-26T23:49:23Z","messageBody":"Three compounding bugs, found and fixed in sequence while matching
the logo to Figma's 223x26 mobile / 758x115 tablet+desktop spec:

1. ZimmLogo took a plain DOM `style` prop, which can only ever hold
   one unconditional value — passing a Chakra responsive array through
   it just stringified to garbage ("223px,,758px,12"). ZimmLogo now
   renders via chakra.svg and accepts an `sx` prop (Chakra's own
   style-prop system, which actually resolves responsive values into
   real media queries) alongside the existing `style` for simple
   static overrides.
2. Even through `sx`, sizing still lost to base SFCC's own `logo` part
   (width: [8,8,8,12] Chakra-spacing array) at md/lg — Chakra's
   multi-part recipe merge combines our Header.css.ts override with
   that base part in a way that isn't a reliable per-key override for
   this specific key, regardless of array vs. fully-named-object
   responsive syntax. Logo sizing now bypasses that merge entirely:
   removed from header.css.ts's `logo` part, set instead as a plain
   HEADER_LOGO_SX object passed directly to <ZimmLogo sx={...}> in
   header/index.tsx — a plain object spread, no base theme involved.
3. ZimmLogo's own base sx sets maxWidth: 327px as a generic default,
   which survived the merge with HEADER_LOGO_SX (that object only set
   width/height) and silently capped the 758px desktop/tablet target.
   HEADER_LOGO_SX now explicitly sets maxWidth: 'none'.

Lifts a real menuExpanded state into the header shell, driven by
whether any desktop/tablet mega-menu popover is currently open —
previously RightBar/LeftBar accepted menuExpanded but nothing set it
(Wave-1 infra only).

useMegaMenuOpenReporter.ts adds a small context + hook: base _app.jsx
constructs Header's `children` (ListMenu) itself, so Header cannot
inject a callback prop into it directly. ListMenu reports "open" via
this context (see previous commit); Header owns closing — either the
pointer leaves the whole topBar row (not just the individual trigger,
so moving toward RightBar's Close control doesn't prematurely close
it), or the Close control itself is clicked.

Mobile L1/L2 wiring is out of scope here (SFCC-97 territory) —
menuExpanded stays 'closed'/'fullSwap' only on this branch.

{"additions":10187,"author":{"id":"MDQ6VXNlcjI5NDcyOTg2","is_bot":false,"login":"TimLavelleACC","name":""},"baseRefName":"develop","baseRefOid":"269d5d40149b9947111dd87e78d37b92fccd4c99","body":"## Summary

Rebuilds the global header per SFCC-52 and its successor stories (SFCC-746 nav bar, SFCC-747 logo). Built as six independently-implemented branches, merged for integrated local testing, plus follow-on Contentful and i18n work done directly on this branch once testing surfaced real gaps.

**Header build (six merged branches):**
- **Beta cherry-pick + cleanup** — `LeftBar`/`RightBar`/`ZimmSearchInput` header decomposition (from `feature/SFCC-52_global-header-ui-beta`), dead `navGroup/` removed.
- **`header-css-tokens`** — co-located `header.ts`/`listMenu.ts` recipes to `header.css.ts`/`list-menu.css.ts`, fixed `NAV_LETTER_SPACING` to `0` per confirmed Figma token.
- **`contentful-navgroup-migration`** — generalised footer's `footerNavGroup` into a shared `navGroup` type (footer + header mega-menu columns); live Contentful `dev` migrated.
- **`sfcc-746-nav-bar`** (SFCC-746) — new `headerNavItem`/`headerNavigation` Contentful types, `useHeaderNav` hook, `ListMenu` self-fetches nav data (placeholder content component pending SFCC-96).
- **`sfcc-747-logo`** (SFCC-747) — fixed header rendering the base template's placeholder icon instead of the real `ZimmLogo` wordmark; verified AC (focus, keyboard, responsive sizing, no Contentful dependency).
- **`header-shell-tests`** — backfilled missing Storybook/Vitest coverage for `LeftBar`/`RightBar`/`list-menu.tsx`/`list-menu-trigger.tsx`.
- **`header-menu-expanded-state`** — shared `MenuExpandedState` contract (`closed`/`fullSwap`/`mobileL1`/`mobileL2`) wired into `LeftBar`/`RightBar`, demoed via Storybook mock toggles.

**Contentful — properly reconciled, not just dev-patched:**
- Merged `feature/contentful-cleanup` (CodeRabbit-approved) — brings `image.js` into the tracked content-types set and removes several dead Contentful components (`button`, `duplexSection`, `collectionHero`, `imageText`, `heroBanner`, `productHero`, `videoEmbed`).
- Added `phoneLabel`/`whatsAppLabel`/`emailLabel` to `footerConfig` (co-located with existing `phoneHref`/`whatsAppHref`/`emailHref` — one editorial unit, not a generic microcopy string), wired through `Footer` → `FooterNavColumn` → `ZimmContactIconRow`.
- Ran a full `sync:contentful` + `install:contentful --target dev` — the org-level Environment Template is now properly version-6, covering `footerConfig`/`headerNavItem`/`headerNavigation`/`image`/`link`/`navGroup`/`region`/`uiCopy`. `navGroup`/`headerNavItem`/`headerNavigation` (previously dev-only via direct API writes) are now genuinely template-managed.
- Closed out the deferred `footerNavGroup` cleanup — hard-deleted the 3 old entries and the content type itself now that `navGroup` fully supersedes it.
- Seeded live `dev` entries so the header renders real nav content end-to-end: 1 `headerNavigation` root + 5 `headerNavItem`s (New/Clothing/Accessories/Collections/Z.Immerse, all direct links).

**i18n — react-intl → uiCopy for Zimmermann-authored chrome:**
- New project policy: react-intl is out for Zimmermann-authored code, all aria-labels/UI chrome text source from Contentful's `uiCopy` type via `useUiCopy()` instead.
- Converted `header/index.tsx`, `leftBar/index.tsx`, `rightBar/index.tsx`, `list-menu/list-menu.tsx` — every `intl.formatMessage({id, defaultMessage})` became `t(key, fallback)`, same key/fallback text, so behaviour is unchanged until an editor overrides a value.
- Extended `useUiCopy`'s `t()` with optional `values` interpolation support (react-intl had this, `uiCopy` didn't — needed for `"My cart, number of items: {numItems}"`).
- Replaced `rightBar`'s direct read of vendor SFCC react-intl content (`messages[link.name]` from `@salesforce/retail-react-app`'s `account/constant.js`) with a local `ACCOUNT_NAV_LABELS` map, so nothing in this component calls `formatMessage` on someone else's descriptors anymore.
- Fixed 6 missing `header.button.assistive_msg.*` translation keys along the way (pre-existing gap, console-warning only, not a behaviour bug).

## Explicitly NOT in this PR — still to do

- **SFCC-93 (scroll behaviour)** — no design AC exists yet; deliberately out of scope.
- **Header region selector** and **3 logo behaviour scenarios (HPC-016)** — no Figma frame provided, out of scope per the implementation plan.

## Known follow-ups (not blocking, flagged for visibility)

- `list-menu.stories.tsx` (from `header-shell-tests`) still tests/demos the old `root`/`categories` prop shape — `ListMenu` now self-fetches via `useHeaderNav()` and ignores those props, so this story renders incorrectly. Needs a rewrite.
- `RightBar`'s Wishlist/Account icon calls commerce hooks directly (`withRegistration`), despite its own JSDoc claiming container/presentational separation — throws without a `CommerceApiProvider` in the tree. Worth a second look before SFCC-96/97 build further on top of it.
- `gallery`/`galleryItem`/`imageAndText` Contentful types exist live in `dev` but are deliberately excluded from the tracked template — a BA's and Tim's own separate testing, not part of this initiative.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- [x] `npm run test` — 22/22 files, 305/305 tests passing
- [x] Verified locally end-to-end: header renders real Contentful-driven nav data, logo/letter-spacing fixes visible, `menuExpanded` states demoed in Storybook (`Layout/Header/LeftBar`, `Layout/Header/RightBar`)
- [x] Live Contentful `dev` verified directly against the CDA (not just the app) after the template rebuild and content seeding
- [ ] Local CodeRabbit review (`cr review --light --base develop`) — not yet run on the merged integration branch
- [ ] Manual cross-breakpoint pass (desktop/tablet/mobile) once SFCC-96/97 land

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_016GTGo4ZCJGFzLwjsqmwitY","messageHeadline":"fix(header): set logo to fixed per-breakpoint dimensions","oid":"61f756ed3bfd321a5828e81930bdd2e9b245fdf8"},{"authoredDate":"2026-08-26T23:49:23Z","authors":[{"email":"tim+1@lavelle.bio","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjY0NDU3MTA=","login":"TimLavelle","name":"TimLavelle"},{"email":"noreply@anthropic.com","id":"MDQ6VXNlcjgxODQ3","login":"claude","name":"Claude Sonnet 5"}],"committedDate":"2026-08-26T23:49:23Z","messageBody":"Three compounding bugs, found and fixed in sequence while matching
the logo to Figma's 223x26 mobile / 758x115 tablet+desktop spec:

1. ZimmLogo took a plain DOM `style` prop, which can only ever hold
   one unconditional value — passing a Chakra responsive array through
   it just stringified to garbage ("223px,,758px,12"). ZimmLogo now
   renders via chakra.svg and accepts an `sx` prop (Chakra's own
   style-prop system, which actually resolves responsive values into
   real media queries) alongside the existing `style` for simple
   static overrides.
2. Even through `sx`, sizing still lost to base SFCC's own `logo` part
   (width: [8,8,8,12] Chakra-spacing array) at md/lg — Chakra's
   multi-part recipe merge combines our Header.css.ts override with
   that base part in a way that isn't a reliable per-key override for
   this specific key, regardless of array vs. fully-named-object
   responsive syntax. Logo sizing now bypasses that merge entirely:
   removed from header.css.ts's `logo` part, set instead as a plain
   HEADER_LOGO_SX object passed directly to <ZimmLogo sx={...}> in
   header/index.tsx — a plain object spread, no base theme involved.
3. ZimmLogo's own base sx sets maxWidth: 327px as a generic default,
   which survived the merge with HEADER_LOGO_SX (that object only set
   width/height) and silently capped the 758px desktop/tablet target.
   HEADER_LOGO_SX now explicitly sets maxWidth: 'none'.

  "id": "17902",
  "key": "SFCC-52",
  "summary": "Global Header UI",
  "customfield_10231": {
    "value": "*Desktop/Mobile:*

# Given a shopper visits any page on the storefront, when the page loads, then the global header is displayed at the top of the page on both desktop and mobile.
# Given a shopper scrolls down the page, when the page is scrolled, then the top navigation remains sticky and visible at the top of the screen.
# Given a shopper clicks the Zimmermann logo, when the click is registered, then the shopper is navigated to the homepage.
# Given a shopper has items in their bag, when they view the header, then the Bag icon displays the correct running count of items.
# Given a bag item is added or removed, when the bag is updated, then the Bag icon count updates without requiring a full page reload.

*Desktop:*

# Given a shopper views the header, when the page loads, then all header icons (Search, Account, Saved, Bag) are visible per the linked Figma Design.

*Mobile:*

# Given a shopper views the site on mobile, when any page loads, then the hamburger icon is displayed top-left in the header alongside Search and Bag icons top-right.
# Given a shopper taps the hamburger icon, when the tap is registered, then the full-screen navigation drawer opens and the hamburger icon is replaced by a close (×) icon.
# Given the navigation drawer is open, when a shopper taps the close (×) icon, then the drawer closes and the hamburger icon is restored.
# Given the navigation drawer is open, when a shopper views it, then all top-level navigation categories are displayed vertically in the correct order per the linked Figma design.
# Given the navigation drawer is open, when a shopper views it, then Saved and Account links are displayed below the main navigation categories."
  }
}

{
  "id": "19197",
  "key": "SFCC-746",
  "summary": "Navigation – PWA Kit & Contentful",
  "customfield_10231": {
    "value": "*Content Type*

# Given the Contentful content type is created, when a Site Merchandiser opens the content model, then it includes nav item label, category ID, display order, and storefront scoping.
# Given a Site Merchandiser updates and publishes the nav entries in Contentful, when the page loads after publishing, then the updated nav items and ordering are reflected across all storefronts without a code deployment.

*Structure — Desktop*

# Given a shopper visits any page on desktop, when the page loads, then the Navigation component renders with top-level nav items displayed left-aligned in the configured order.
# Given a shopper visits any page on desktop, when the page loads, then Search Bar, Account, Wishlist and Bag icons are displayed right-aligned in the nav bar.
# Given a shopper opens a mega menu on desktop, when the mega menu is active, then the four icons are replaced by a CLOSE X control on the right side of the nav
# Given a shopper clicks CLOSE X on desktop, when the control is activated, then the mega menu is dismissed and the four icons are restored.

*Structure — Tablet*

# Given a shopper visits any page on tablet, when the page loads, then the Navigation component renders with all top-level nav items and all four icons visible (Search, Account, Wishlist, Bag)
# Given a shopper opens a mega menu on tablet, when the mega menu is active, then the four icons are replaced by CLOSE X on the right side of the nav.
# Given a shopper clicks CLOSE X on tablet, when the control is activated, then the mega menu is dismissed and the four icons are restored.

*Structure — Mobile*

# Given a shopper visits any page on mobile, when the page loads, then the Navigation component renders with a hamburger icon on the left and Search and Bag icons on the right. Top-level nav items are not visible.
# Given a shopper opens the mobile drawer, when the drawer is active, then the hamburger icon is replaced by a close icon on the left. Search and Bag icons remain visible on the right.
# Given a shopper taps the close icon on mobile, when activated, then the mobile drawer is dismissed and the hamburger icon is restored.

*Category Taxonomy*

# Given the Navigation component renders, when it reads top-level nav items, then items, their display order, and storefront visibility are managed in Contentful using a category ID to reference the SFCC category taxonomy in BM (SFCC-28) and are not hardcoded in the component.
# Given a nav item corresponds to an SFCC category, when a shopper clicks it, then they are navigated to the corresponding category PLP.
# Given the Navigation component fetches top-level nav items from Contentful, when it renders, then it uses the storefront-specific configuration ensuring nav items and their ordering reflect the correct regional setup.
# Given a nav item is unpublished or not configured in Contentful for a specific storefront, when the Navigation component renders on that storefront, then the corresponding nav item does not appear in the headline nav.

*Search*

# Given a shopper clicks the search icon in the header, when the interaction occurs, then they are navigated to the search experience - [https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-113|https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-113|smart-link] 

*Wishlist*

# Given a shopper views the header and their wishlist is empty, when the component renders, then the wishlist icon displays in its outlined state.
# Given a shopper views the header and their wishlist contains one or more items, when the component renders, then the wishlist icon displays in its filled state.

*Cart*

# Given a shopper views the header, when the cart contains items, then the cart icon displays a dynamic item count — full cart behaviour is covered in the dynamic cart header story - [https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-827|https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-827|smart-link] 

*Accessibility*

# Given a screen reader user is navigating by landmarks, when they reach the main navigation, then it is wrapped in a nav element with aria-label equal to Main navigation, distinguishing it from any other nav regions on the page.
# Given a screen reader user navigates the headline nav, when they move through the top-level items, then each item is announced correctly and the number of items is communicated via a list structure.
# Given a keyboard-only user is navigating the header on desktop or tablet, when they Tab through the headline nav, then each top-level item and icon receives focus in left-to-right order.
# Given a screen reader user navigates to a top-level item that triggers a mega menu, when the item receives focus and the menu is closed, then the item is announced with aria-haspopup true and aria-expanded false.
# Given a screen reader user activates a mega menu trigger, when the menu opens, then aria-expanded updates to true and the CLOSE X control is focusable and announced as Close menu.
# Given a screen reader user navigates to Z.IMMERSE, when the item receives focus, then it is announced as a standard link with no aria-haspopup or aria-expanded attributes.
# Given a keyboard-only user is on mobile with the drawer closed, when they Tab to the hamburger button, then it is announced as Open navigation menu with aria-expanded false.
# Given a keyboard-only user opens the mobile drawer, when the drawer is active, then the close icon is announced as Close navigation menu with aria-expanded true.
# Given a keyboard-only user is interacting with the nav on any device, when they interact with any element, then all interactions are achievable without a mouse."
  }
}

{
  "id": "19207",
  "key": "SFCC-747",
  "summary": "Logo Masthead – PWA Kit Component",
  "customfield_10231": {
    "value": "*Structure — Desktop*
1. Given a shopper visits any page on desktop, when the page loads, then the Logo Masthead component renders the Zimmermann wordmark left-aligned in the header at the desktop size, consistent with the Figma design.
2. Given a shopper visits any page on desktop, when the logo renders, then it sits in its own row below the top-level navigation bar, not inline with the nav items.

*Structure — Tablet*
3. Given a shopper visits any page on tablet, when the page loads, then the Logo Masthead component renders the Zimmermann wordmark left-aligned in the header at the tablet size, consistent with the Figma design.
4. Given a shopper visits any page on tablet, when the logo renders, then it sits in its own row below the top-level navigation bar, consistent with desktop behaviour.

*Structure — Mobile*
5. Given a shopper visits any page on mobile, when the page loads, then the Logo Masthead component renders the Zimmermann wordmark left-aligned in the header at the mobile size, consistent with the Figma design.

*Link Behaviour*
6. Given a shopper clicks the logo on any page, when the click is registered, then they are navigated to the homepage of the active storefront.
7. Given a shopper is already on the homepage, when they click the logo, then the page reloads or no navigation occurs — the logo does not navigate away from the homepage unexpectedly.

*Accessibility*
8. Given a screen reader user navigates to the logo, when the logo receives focus, then the logo image is announced as Zimmermann via alt text on the img element, or aria-label on an inline SVG with role=img.
9. Given a screen reader user navigates to the logo link, when the link receives focus, then the link is announced as Zimmermann, go to homepage so the destination is clear.
10. Given a keyboard-only user is navigating the header, when they Tab to the logo, then the logo link is the first focusable element in the header, before any navigation items or icons.
11. Given a keyboard-only user tabs to the logo link, when it receives focus, then a visible focus ring is displayed that meets WCAG 2.1 AA contrast requirements (minimum 3:1 ratio against adjacent colours)."
  }
}

{
  "id": "18141",
  "key": "SFCC-96",
  "summary": "Expanded Navigation - PWA Kit and Contentful",
  "customfield_10231": {
    "value": "+*Content Type*+

*AC1: Contentful content type*

* Given the Contentful content type is created, when a Site Merchandiser opens the content model, then it includes nav item label, link/slug, item type (subcategory or editorial), display order, campaign image, and storefront scoping.

*AC2: Contentful authoring*

* Given a Site Merchandiser creates or updates a nav entry in Contentful and publishes it, when the page loads after publishing, then the updated links, ordering, or imagery are reflected across all breakpoints without a code deployment.

+*Structure - Desktop*+

*AC3: Mega menu trigger — desktop*

* Given a shopper is on desktop and hovers over or clicks a top-level nav item that triggers a mega menu (NEW, CLOTHING, ACCESSORIES, COLLECTIONS), when the interaction occurs, then the mega menu panel renders below the navigation bar overlaying the page content.

*AC4: Mega menu layout — desktop*

* Given the mega menu is open on desktop, when it renders, then it displays a left panel of sub-category text links and editorial links organised in rows and a right panel containing a full-height editorial image.

*AC5: Collections two-column layout — desktop*

* Given the Collections category is active on desktop, when the mega menu opens, then sub-category links in the left panel are displayed in two columns with group headings (READY TO WEAR, SWIM & RESORT).

*AC6: Page overlay — desktop*

* Given the mega menu is open on desktop, when it renders, then a semi-transparent dark overlay is applied to the page content beneath the panel.

*AC7: Active nav item underline — desktop*

* Given the mega menu is open, when a top-level nav item is triggering the mega menu, then that nav item is displayed with an underline indicating it is active.

+*Structure — Tablet*+

*AC8: Mega menu trigger — tablet*

* Given a shopper is on tablet and hovers over or clicks a top-level nav item that triggers a mega menu, when the interaction occurs, then the mega menu panel renders below the navigation bar overlaying the page content.

*AC9: Mega menu layout — tablet*

* Given the mega menu is open on tablet, when it renders, then it displays sub-category text links and editorial on top, with a full width editorial image below.

*AC10: Collections two-column layout — tablet* 

* Given the Collections category is active on tablet, when the mega menu opens, then sub-category links are displayed in two columns with group headings (READY TO WEAR, SWIM & RESORT).

*AC11: Page overlay — tablet*

* Given the mega menu is open on tablet, when it renders, then a semi-transparent dark overlay is applied to the page content beneath the panel

*AC12: Active nav item underline — tablet*

* Given the mega menu is open, when a top-level nav item is triggering the mega menu, then that nav item is displayed with an underline indicating it is active.

+*Structure — Mobile*+

*AC13: Mobile menu trigger*

* Given a shopper is on mobile and taps the hamburger icon (≡), when the interaction occurs, then the mobile menu drawer opens as a full-width overlay displaying all top-level nav items (NEW, CLOTHING, ACCESSORIES, COLLECTIONS, Z.IMMERSE) as large heading-level links.

*AC14: Mobile menu — Wishlist and Account*

* Given the mobile menu drawer is open, when it renders, then Wishlist (with dynamic item count if applicable) and Account links are displayed below the top-level nav items.

*AC15: Mobile menu — close icon*

* Given the mobile menu drawer is open, when the shopper taps the close icon (×), then the drawer dismisses and the hamburger icon (≡) is restored.

*AC16: Mobile menu — no mega menu*

* Given a shopper taps a top-level nav item on mobile, when the interaction occurs, then the shopper is navigated directly to the corresponding category PLP - no mega menu panel renders on mobile.

+*Dismiss Behaviour*+

*AC17: Mega menu stays open while cursor is within panel*

* Given the mega menu is open on desktop or tablet, when the shopper's cursor remains within either the triggering nav item or the mega menu panel, then the mega menu stays open.

*AC18: Mega menu dismisses on cursor exit*

* Given the mega menu is open on desktop or tablet, when the shopper's cursor leaves both the triggering nav item and the mega menu panel boundary, then the mega menu dismisses.

*AC19: Dismiss via CLOSE X*

* Given the mega menu is open on desktop or tablet, when the shopper clicks CLOSE X in the nav bar, then the mega menu dismisses and the nav icons are restored.

*AC20: Dismiss via Escape*

* Given the mega menu is open, when the shopper presses Escape, then the mega menu dismisses and focus returns to the triggering nav item.

*AC21: Dismiss on sub-category link click*

* Given the mega menu is open, when the shopper clicks a sub-category link or editorial link, then they are navigated to the correct destination and the mega menu dismisses.

*AC22: Z.IMMERSE — no mega menu*

* Given a shopper hovers over or clicks Z.IMMERSE on desktop or tablet, when the interaction occurs, then no mega menu appears and the shopper is navigated directly to the Z.IMMERSE destination page.

+*Sub-category & Editorial Links*+

*AC23: Sub-category links driven by BM via Contentful category ID*

* Given the mega menu renders for a nav item, when the left panel loads, then sub-category links are fetched from the SFCC category taxonomy via the BM catalogue using the category ID stored in Contentful and are not hardcoded in the component.

*AC24: Editorial links driven by Contentful*

* Given the mega menu renders for a nav item, when the left panel loads, then editorial links are fetched from Contentful for that nav item using the active storefront and are not hardcoded in the component.

*AC25: Sub-category link navigation*

* Given a sub-category link is clicked, when the shopper selects it, then they are navigated to the corresponding category PLP.

*AC26: Editorial link navigation*

* Given an editorial link is clicked, when the shopper selects it, then they are navigated to the corresponding destination page.

*AC27: Offline sub-category hidden*

* Given a sub-category is set to offline in Business Manager for the active storefront, when the mega menu renders, then the corresponding sub-category link does not appear.

*AC28: Editorial link hidden when unpublished*

* Given an editorial link is unpublished or not configured in Contentful for the active storefront, when the mega menu renders, then the corresponding editorial link does not appear.

+*Editorial Image*+

*AC29: Editorial image driven by Contentful*

* Given the mega menu renders for a nav item, when the right panel loads, then the editorial image is fetched from Contentful for that nav item using the active storefront's locale and is not hardcoded in the component.

*AC30: Editorial image fallback*

* Given Contentful content has not been authored or a fetch fails, when the right panel attempts to render, then the editorial image slot does not render and the mega menu remains functional with sub-category links only.

+*Accessibility*+

*AC31: Keyboard and screen reader operability*

* Given a keyboard-only user is interacting with the mega menu, when they navigate and dismiss it, then all interactions are achievable without a mouse and focus is managed correctly throughout.

*AC32: Screen reader state announcement*

* Given a screen reader user is interacting with the mega menu, when they navigate it, then the open/closed state and all links are correctly announced.

*AC33: Reduced motion*

* Given a user has enabled reduced motion at OS level, when the mega menu opens or closes, then any animation respects the reduced motion preference."
  }
}

{
  "id": "18142",
  "key": "SFCC-97",
  "summary": "Expanded Navigation (Mobile) - PWA Kit Component",
  "customfield_10231": {
    "value": "# Given a shopper is on mobile, when they tap the hamburger icon, then the navigation panel opens and displays top-level categories.
# Given the navigation panel is open, when the shopper taps a category that has subcategories, then the panel transitions to display the subcategory list for that category.
# Given the shopper has drilled into a subcategory level, when they tap the back control, then the panel returns to the previous level.
# Given the navigation panel is open, when the shopper taps a destination link, then the panel closes and the shopper is navigated to the correct page.
# Given the nav includes Z.Immerse, when the shopper taps it, then no drill-down occurs and they are navigated directly to the Z.Immerse page.
# Given the nav includes 'Back in Boutique', when the shopper taps it, then they are navigated directly to the relevant page.
# Given a shopper taps outside the open navigation panel, when the tap event fires, then the panel closes.
# Given a site merchandiser adds or removes a nav item in the CMS, when the storefront renders, then the navigation reflects the change without a code deployment.
# Given a category panel is open, when the shopper views it, then a campaign image is displayed in the content slot as configured in the CMS; if no image is configured, the slot is empty and the layout does not break.
# Given a screen reader user focuses on the hamburger icon, when it receives focus, then it is announced with its expanded/collapsed state.
# Given a screen reader user is within an open navigation panel, when they navigate the links, then each link is announced with its label and destination."
  }
}

                aria-label={t('header.button.assistive_msg.logo', 'Logo')}
                variant="unstyled"
                onClick={onLogoClick}
                __css={styles.logoButton}
              >
                {/* SFCC-747: real wordmark, sized via HEADER_LOGO_SX above — previously rendered
                    the base template's placeholder BrandLogo icon. `sx`, not `style`: a plain
                    DOM style attribute can't express Chakra's responsive breakpoint values. */}
                <ZimmLogo sx={HEADER_LOGO_SX} />
              </Button>
            </chakra.div>
          )}

          {/* Mobile-only search — commented out, pending searchPopover implementation */}
          {/* <HideOnDesktop display={{ base: 'block', lg: 'none' }}><SearchBar /></HideOnDesktop> */}
        </chakra.div>
      </chakra.header>
